title: Jawaharlal Nehru at Washington Press Club: Non-Alignment is Not Neutrality in Injustice (1949)
summary: During his 1949 state visit to the United States, Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru addressed the National Press Club in Washington, eloquently defining India's foreign policy of non-alignment.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 153: நேருவும் வாஷிங்டன் செய்தியாளர் மன்றமும்: “இந்தப் புத்தகத்தின் பெயரைச் சொல்ல முடியவில்லை!”
full_text:
In October 1949, Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru stepped to the rostrum at the National Press Club in Washington, D.C., during his first official state visit to the United States.

The Cold War was crystallizing into rigid binary alliances between Washington and Moscow. A prominent American journalist pressed Nehru on India's refusal to sign military pacts:
"Prime Minister Nehru, the free world is locked in an existential struggle against totalitarian communism. Where does India stand? Is your policy of non-alignment merely passive neutrality, an evasion of global moral responsibility? In international affairs, if you are not with us, are you not with our adversaries?"

Nehru paused, adjusting the rose in his achkan, and replied with ringing philosophical clarity:
"Sir, you misunderstand the essence of India's stance. Where freedom is menaced, or where justice is threatened, or where aggression takes place, India cannot and shall never be neutral!

What we reject is the tragic illusion that the world must be carved into antagonistic military blocs armed for mutual destruction. India has emerged from two centuries of foreign subjugation; we did not win our sovereignty merely to become a camp-follower of any distant power! Non-alignment is not passive isolationism; it is positive, active independence of judgment. We reserve the sacred right to judge every global issue on its own moral merits and its contribution to world peace. That is not cowardice; it is the courage of conviction!"

The audience of seasoned foreign correspondents broke into sustained applause. Nehru had articulated a foundational doctrine that would guide the newly decolonized nations of the Global South for decades.

moral: Moral independence is not indifference; true integrity assesses issues by the standard of universal justice rather than partisan pressure.
